title: The internal-Hom comparison for a bounded free model
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. On the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ take the constant coefficient ring sheaf $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ and its module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $P'$ be a bounded cochain complex whose terms are finite free $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules, meaning isomorphic to finite direct sums of $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$, and let $N$ be a bounded cochain complex of $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with the constant coefficient identification and exact module pullback $
u_T^*$ of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Use derived internal Hom on each of these ringed sites [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The canonical evaluation comparison
$$

u_T^*R\mathcal Hom_A(P',N)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(
u_T^*P',
u_T^*N)
$$
is an isomorphism. Here the comparison is the one induced by pulling back evaluation: under the canonical bounded finite-free Hom-complex models [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model], it is induced by the termwise maps $
u_T^*\mathcal Hom_A(P'^i,N^j)	o\mathcal Hom_A(
u_T^*P'^i,
u_T^*N^j)$ obtained by currying the pullback of $\mathcal Hom_A(P'^i,N^j)\otimes_A P'^i	o N^j$ [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. The second variable requires no etale finite-Tor hypothesis. Use the size convention of [def-weil-size-convention], so that the two coefficient sites are small in the universe used for module sheaves.

proof.text: Write $F=\nu_T^*$, $R=A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ and $S=A_{T,\mathrm{proet}}$. The exact comparison-pullback lemma identifies $F(R)$ with $S$ and says that $F$ is additive and exact and sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus its action on the derived category is computed termwise. An additive functor preserves a finite biproduct: apply it to the equations $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i=1$. In particular $F(R^{\oplus r})\cong S^{\oplus r}$, including $r=0$. The complexes $FP'$ and $FN$ have the same termwise support bounds as $P'$ and $N$, since $F(0)=0$.

proof.text: For a finite-free term $M=R^{\oplus r}$ and any module sheaf $B$, evaluation on the basis gives $\mathcal Hom_R(M,B)\cong B^{\oplus r}$: on each slice a linear map is uniquely specified by the images of the $r$ basis sections, and restriction restricts those images. This proves the module identity used in the blueprint for arbitrary $B$, without applying the finite-Tor-only statement of lem-sf-hom-finite-projective. Curry the pulled-back evaluation using the module tensor comparison and tensor-Hom adjunction. The resulting $c_{M,B}:F\mathcal Hom_R(M,B)\to\mathcal Hom_S(FM,FB)$ is, in these coordinates and the identifications of step 1, the identity on $(FB)^{\oplus r}$: evaluation of $(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ on the $i$th basis vector is $b_i$ on both sides. Thus $c_{M,B}$ is an isomorphism. These maps commute with postcomposition and precomposition: after evaluation the two postcomposition composites send $(h,x)$ to $v(h(x))$, and the two precomposition composites send $(h,x)$ to $h(u(x))$. The natural tensor comparison and injectivity of currying identify the respective maps. This argument works for all maps of the finite-free terms, including matrices of nonconstant sections. For a term $M$ given only with an isomorphism $e:R^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\sim}M$, precomposition with $e$ and with $Fe$ conjugates $c_{M,B}$ to $c_{R^{\oplus r},B}$ by the precomposition identity just proved. Hence the conclusion holds for the actual terms of $P'$ and is independent of their chosen bases.

proof.text: Choose $u\leq v$ with $P'^i=0$ outside $[u,v]$. For the Hom complex $H=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P',N)$, its degree $m$ product has only these finitely many potentially nonzero factors, so $H^m=\bigoplus_{i=u}^v\mathcal Hom_R(P'^i,N^{i+m})$. Its differential is $(dh)^i=d_Nh^i-(-1)^m h^{i+1}d_{P'}$. Apply $F$ and its finite-biproduct comparison from step 1; the direct sum of the isomorphisms $c_{P'^i,N^{i+m}}$ of step 2 gives $C^m:(FH)^m\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom^m_S(FP',FN)$. The two differential terms commute separately by the postcomposition and precomposition equations of step 2; additivity of $F$ preserves subtraction and $(-1)^m$. Hence $C$ is a chain isomorphism. This is the finite total-complex calculation in the blueprint: if $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P',R[0])$, its degree $r$ term is $(P'^{-r})^\vee$, with $d_D\phi=(-1)^{r+1}\phi d_{P'}$; the corresponding map $D^r\otimes N^s\to H^{r+s}$ sends $\phi\otimes n$ to the map $x\mapsto(-1)^{rs}\phi(x)n$ on $P'^{-r}$ and to zero on other terms. The postcomposition signs agree because $r+r(s+1)=rs$ modulo $2$, and the precomposition signs agree because $(r+1)s+r+1=rs+r+s+1$. Thus the dual uses degree $-r$, correcting the un-reversed dual index in the blueprint.

proof.text: Use the small skeletons in the common size convention. Apply the bounded-free derived-Hom-model lemma on $(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ to $(P',N)$: $P'$ is bounded above, $N$ bounded below, and a finite-free term is a summand of itself via the identity maps. It gives the canonical isomorphism $QH\cong R\mathcal Hom_R(QP',QN)$. Apply the same lemma on $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},S)$ to $(FP',FN)$, whose bounds and finite-free terms were checked in step 1. Since $F$ sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, the first canonical model pulls back to $Q(FH)$. Localizing the chain isomorphism $C$ of step 3 and composing these canonical model isomorphisms therefore gives an isomorphism between the two objects in the statement. Neither application asks for flatness, projectivity, or finite Tor amplitude of $N$ or $FN$.

Put $H_S=\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(FP',FN)$ and write $a_R:Q_RH\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_R(Q_RP',Q_RN)$ and $a_S:Q_SH_S\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_S(Q_SFP',Q_SFN)$ for the canonical models of step 4. Let $F_D$ be the functor on derived categories induced by $F$, and identify $F_DQ_R$ with $Q_SF$ as in step 1. The concrete Hom-model specification of the comparison in the statement is the composite $a_S\circ Q_S(C)\circ(F_Da_R)^{-1}$. To check its evaluation description, on each tensor summand $H^m\otimes_R P'^i$ evaluation is projection to $\mathcal Hom_R(P'^i,N^{i+m})$ followed by module evaluation, with value $h^i(x)$. The defining currying equation of step 2 says that evaluation following $C^m$ on $FP'^i$ equals $F$ of this evaluation, after the module tensor comparison. Equality on these summands gives equality of the total evaluation maps. Evaluation is a chain map because $(dh)(x)+(-1)^m h(dx)=d_N(h(x))$, with the two precomposition terms cancelling by step 3. Under the K-injective description of derived internal Hom, postcomposition with the specified resolution map $\eta_N:N\to I(N)$ respects this identity term by term: $(\eta_N\circ h^i)(x)=\eta_N(h^i(x))$; the identical equation applies to the resolution of $FN$. Thus the representative evaluations are compatible with the canonical model identifications, and the displayed composite is the specified evaluation comparison. Each of its three factors is invertible by steps 3 and 4.
